body.objective: Determine whether the exact minimal Krein lift of the eight-point profile can be identified with the purely negatively charged, trace-null Q remainder in Bateman-Turok Eq. 19.
activates: an exact charge generator on the forced cross-Krein fibre
a charge decomposition of the fourth-profile forward block
a fail-closed Eq. 19 Q-remainder identification test
body.current_gate: KREIN_CHARGE_LOCALIZATION: diagonalize the invariant charge action of G_missing(rho), project the canonical negative line used by the fourth-profile lift, and determine which charge sectors generate its nonzero pullback.
body.stop_condition: Land an exact certificate with an independent verifier that proves or refutes identification with the one-sided negative-charge radical, preserves the finite order-lambda Eq. 19 boundary, and does not call fibre charge algebra a full operator theorem.
body.forbid: no basis-dependent charge claim without conjugating the generator; no nonzero negative norm assigned to a one-sided null charge line; no algebraic fibre result called an all-order projector pushforward, generalized-Born trace, probability, gravity/BRST lift, or LORENTZIAN-CAUSAL theorem
body.resource_hint: For G=[[0,-rho],[-rho,-2]], use null charge columns n_plus=(1,0) and n_minus=(1,-rho). Their matrix S gives S^T G S=rho^2 J and transports diag(1,-1) to H_G. Project f2=(0,1), then test the self- and cross-pairings of Pi_plus f2 and Pi_minus f2. Apply the same projectors to both hard-profile amplitudes.
